name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Mullin's fundraising advantage against an opponent with no reported money
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 97 percent
No public polling, leaving wider residual uncertainty
model.rationale: A D+26 district, an incumbent holding a large fundraising edge over a challenger with no reported money, and markets at 97 percent Democratic all point the same way. The absence of polling keeps residual uncertainty wide, but the structural advantage is decisive.
model.watch: Any surprise would likely come from a turnout anomaly or late outside spending, neither of which has materialized in this low-information race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 15th District, centered in San Mateo County south of San Francisco, leans Democratic by roughly 26 points and ranks among the bluest House seats in the country. Incumbent Kevin Mullin enters the general election with the advantages of a safe seat: name recognition from prior state service, about $820,000 raised, and no measurable outside spending against him. Republican Charles Hoelter has reported no fundraising and starts with steep structural odds in a district where Democratic margins routinely exceed twenty points.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings follow the race, so the outlook rests on partisanship, incumbency, and resources. Prediction markets price Mullin's chances at about 97 percent. An upset would require a shift far beyond anything seen in recent cycles here, and the expectation is a comfortable double-digit win for Mullin.
